<u>International Harvester Corporation (IH)</u>. IH recommends against the decreased use of sound deadening materials.
American Motors Corporation (AMC). AMC responded to the NHTSA request for comments on noise levels by describing the various noise sources or their vehicles. They anticipate an increase in the size of their mufflers to reduce back pressure related to fuel economy. It was pointed out that the increased size of the muffler is also related to noise regulations. They claim this increased size will add weight to their vehicles.
Summary. Ford stated that the increased use of diesels will increase the noise levels of trucks. IH stated that removing sound deadening material from trucks will increase noise levels. FEA stated that noise levels will increase as power to weight ratios are reduced. AMC claims that reducing the back pressure of exhaust systems will lead to weight increases for larger mufflers to control noise.
Analysis. No market penetration of diesel engines in trucks in MY 1979 was included in the preparation of the fuel economy standard. Therefore, no consequential environmental impact was anticipated for MY 1979. NHTSA
